decisions.quote:
In conclusion, as in Part I of the present study, we could replicate the seminal work
by Langer and Roth (1975), showing that the emphasis of success at the beginning of a
run enhances participants’ estimation of their ability to predict outcomes of a coin toss.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly conclude that both experiments successfully replicated the illusion-of-control effect of Langer and Roth (1975). The shipped 'mixed' coding conflated the replicated original effect with the failure of the novel hypothesis testing whether the illusion of control modulates post-loss speeding.

corrected_value.title: A direct and conceptual replication of post-loss speeding when gambling.
corrected_value.authors: Eben, C., Chen, Z., Vermeylen, L., Billieux, J., & Verbruggen, F.

decisions.quote:
Across experi-
ments, we could again replicate the finding by Langer and Roth (1975) in an online ex-
perimental setting (see also our replication study). Thus, introducing a start response
did not alter the illusion-of-control effect. Moreover, we replicated the finding that par-
ticipants speed up after losses compared to wins (Eben et al., 2020; Verbruggen et al.,
2017).
decisions.reason: Both experiments explicitly re-test and successfully replicate the post-loss speeding effect using the start-response procedure and exclusion criteria of Eben et al. (2020). Under the replication-chain rule, Eben et al. (2020) is the nearest target in the chain re-testing Verbruggen et al. (2017) and is an omitted target in the shipped dataset.

parent_source_inspection.note: Checked quoted conclusion and surrounding target-specific comparisons; new extension hypotheses distinguished from original retested findings.
